column1: # The starting violation list of Broiler.RegEx's architecture tests: every violation that a rule SL1 to SL10 or a
# contract check C1, C3 or C5 of rules.register.json finds in the library on the day the tests were filed, 2026-10-25,
# at work package SJL-11.2 of the shared JavaScript libraries programme, at the code 0.1.0-preview.4 was packed from.
# Broiler.VM's JSD-0081 (section X3) lists the conventions these breach, and requirements R1 to R11 close them.
# Each rule's test asserts its rows in both directions: a violation the rule finds that is not here fails it, and so
# does a row the rule no longer finds. A change that removes a violation removes its row in the same change; no change
# adds one. SJL-11.2 shrinks the list to none, and bundle sjl-11-001's check E-3 holds it empty at the candidate reading.
# Where a rule reads where a violation is - SL1's assembly half, SL3, SL4 and C5 from the IL and the PDB's sequence
# points, SL5 from the NoWarn and WarningsNotAsErrors elements of the project file and of every build file of the
# repository its evaluation imports - its test asserts the row place by place as well: every place the rule finds is
# cited once, and every cited place is one the rule finds, so a row the rule still finds but at no place fails too. A
# call of a listed member in a statement of its own is a new place and fails the test, and so does a citation left on a
# line that no longer holds the violation, although the row's wording is the same in both. A place has two limits, which
# AssemblyFacts states: it is a statement, so a second use inside a statement that already holds one is not a new place;
# and it is where an instruction names the member, its declaring type or a type operand, so a use that names a type or
# an assembly only in a signature, a field or local type or a generic argument is no place at all. Review sees those
# uses. Every other row's violation names its one place: a static field, a public member or type, a file, a package, a
# setting.
# Columns, tab-separated: the rule or check; the violation, exactly as the rule words it; a token the source holds where
# the violation is; and the places, path:line, space-separated, one line of each (a statement can span several).
# RuleRegisterTests checks that each cited line holds the token, so a citation moves with the code; the rule's own test
# decides whether the violation, and each place of it, is still there. A comment line here names a row's repair.
#rule
# Task 2.4c (2026-10-26) re-words three C1 rows, which adds no violation: RegexMatch and RegexGroup moved from
# Broiler.Regex.Matching to Broiler.Regex when the old backend's namespace was deleted (decision D12, requirement R8;
# a break docs/suppressions.md lists), so the rows of Matches, RegexMatch.Groups and RegexMatch.NamedGroups name the
# moved type where they named Broiler.Regex.Matching.RegexMatch. They are the same three violations, which task 2.9
# closes with the surface of 0.2.0-preview.1 (0.1.0-preview.6 by the owner's decision of 2026-11-01; closed, below).
# Task 2.6 (2026-10-27) removes the two C1 rows of BroilerRegex.GroupNames and RegexParser.GroupNames: requirement R6
# reshapes both from a dictionary of each name to one group into the library's own RegexGroupNames, since ES2025 lets
# several groups share a name (a break docs/suppressions.md lists), so neither names a collection in a public signature.
# Task 2.7 (2026-10-27) removes two places of the SL4 row, Broiler.Regex/RegexFlags.cs:90 and :94: RegexFlagsParser.Parse
# now reads the grammar of Text/RegexFlagsText.cs and builds its two messages, unchanged, by concatenating a code unit,
# which reads no culture. The row's other places are the parser's and CharSet's.
# Task 2.8 (2026-10-27) removes the parser's seven places of the SL4 row, Broiler.Regex/Parsing/RegexParser.cs:207,
# :518, :526, :682, :1149, :1468 and :1836: every refusal of the parser is now built by RegexParser.Refuse with its
# diagnostic code, and its message, unchanged, concatenates its values, a number through NumberFormatInfo.InvariantInfo,
# which reads no culture. The row's one place left is CharSet's, the check of the public CharSet.AddRange, which no
# compilation reaches with a range out of order: the parser refuses one itself, at the range's position, before it adds.
# Task 2.9 (2026-11-01) removes the C3 row of RegexSyntaxException: the type is internal and derives from ArgumentException,
# the exception the string-bearing constructors document for a pattern or flags text the specification refuses (their
# broken precondition, convention 3); Compile, the validate entry and RegexFlagsText.Parse answer the refusal as the
# syntax status with its diagnostic.
# Task 2.9 (2026-11-01) removes the last SL4 row and nine C1 rows. The syntax tree (Broiler.Regex.Ast), the parser
# (Broiler.Regex.Parsing.RegexParser) and Broiler.Regex.Unicode.UnicodeCharSets are internal: their public members named
# collections and a delegate (convention 1), and their operations, whose work grows with the pattern or the sets, took
# no meter (convention 4); neither engine's adapter reads them (plan rows 5.2 and 6.1), and the members that do, Compile
# and the validate entry, answer statuses. CharSet.CheckRange, the SL4 row's one place, builds its message through
# NumberFormatInfo.InvariantInfo.
# Task 2.9 (2026-11-01) removes the last three C1 rows, those of the string-bearing result decision D12 keeps:
# RegexMatch.Groups is a ReadOnlySpan<RegexGroup>, RegexMatch.GroupNamed(name) answers a name's group where the
# NamedGroups dictionary did, and BroilerRegex.NextMatch(match) answers the global iteration's next match where Matches'
# IEnumerable did. No C1 row remains.
# Task 2.9 (2026-11-01) removes the seven SL5 rows: Broiler.Regex/Broiler.Regex.csproj resets NoWarn to the SDK's own
# codes, so the packaging props' XML-documentation codes no longer reach the library, and every public member is
# documented (convention 15), a missing comment a build error.
# Task 2.9 (2026-11-01) removes the two SL8 rows: assurance.config.json uses the strict exemption predicate and forbids
# preprocessor directives, Broiler.VM's own settings as Broiler.Unicode's configuration holds them; the three fields the
# strict predicate newly counts as relevant carry their annotations. The list holds no row: row 2.9's check, the
# violation list is empty, holds.
